From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara@acmeanalytics.com>, Tom Lee <tlee@novusplatform.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 slate alignment + QBR readiness runbook

Team — kicking off an aligned pass on the Q3 slate and the QBR runbook. Goal is to lock measurable OKRs, owners, and the pre-QBR evidence checklist by EOD today so we can circulate the packet to execs tomorrow morning.

Quick summary / asks:
- Attached: Q3_OKR_draft_v3.xlsx — contains proposed OKRs with owner columns and success metrics.
- Attached: QBR_runbook_outline.md — timeline, required artifacts, and dry-run schedule.
- Please: 1) add any owner changes inline in the spreadsheet, 2) flag any risky targets with a short comment, 3) confirm availability for the runbook dry-run (Thu 5/17 10–11am PT).

Key constraints to keep in mind:
- We need the new runtime batching improvement (deliverable from infra) to be scoped into the cost-reduction KR — if it slips we should lower the throughput-backed target accordingly.
- Acme (Sara) has asked for a short call in the QBR to review the latency SLAs; Tom from Novus will be present as a partner update.

I’m assigning owners in the sheet where we’ve already agreed; please make edits and reply with explicit approval or escalation notes. If you can’t finish today, tell me your blocker now so we can triage.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Sr. PM, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q3_OKR_draft_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), QBR_runbook_outline.md (text)

Thanks Dylan — I reviewed the sheet and made small owner swaps for the \"Dedup + Cache\" KR (moved owner to Lauren for QA). I also added a comment on the cost KR about the infra dependency and suggested a contingency target if the batching change is delayed.

On the runbook: I can lead the dry-run facilitation on Thu 5/17 10–11am PT. Recommend we reserve the second 30 minutes for the Acme/Novus breakout so we don't eat into the exec slot.

Kimberly Park

Dylan / Kim — made a few substantive updates in the OKR sheet:
- Moved the \"Customer latency 99th\" KR to a partner-facing KR with joint success criteria for Acme (Sara) and Novus (Tom). Added Tom to the related notes so the partner update aligns with the QBR agenda.
- Reduced the cost-saving target from 18% to 14% in the contingency row; left a comment with the rationale (risk: batching release date variability).
- Proposed backup owners for the infra-dependent tasks (Marcus and Irene listed as fallbacks).

I also updated the runbook timeline to add a 48-hour window for evidence collection before the QBR packet freeze. That should give CS time to gather customer-facing slides and metrics.

If the leadership team is comfortable with the contingency move, I'm okay signing off on the owners. Marking my approval in the sheet (comment: Lauren — OK to proceed w/ contingency).

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turn here. I reviewed the contingency and the owner fallbacks. Two asks before I sign off: 1) add a short risk mitigation sentence under the cost KR (who will pause the rollout if early telemetry is negative?), and 2) confirm that the Acme latency segment will be included in the evidence pack (Sara, can you confirm CS will include that graph).

If those are addressed I will sign off on the slate and give the go-ahead to lock the QBR packet. Jonas — please confirm executive packet distribution list once we lock the packet freeze (include legal and security reviewers).
